# Ogg Opus independent PCM fixtures

Original synthetic signals generated by `generate.py`, licensed under this
repository's MIT license. No speech, downloaded media or third-party recordings.
Each channel contains distinct harmonic mixtures and an evolving envelope.
All recordings are 240 ms at 48 kHz. Encoding and reference decoding used
ffmpeg 9.0.2 with libopus 1.6.1, explicitly selecting the libopus reference
decoder. ffmpeg is a development fixture tool, never a runtime dependency.

Run `python3 generate.py` in a serial development workload to regenerate the
Ogg files and canonical interleaved little-endian float32 reference PCM.
Tool versions/container serials may change binary hashes; `manifest.json`
records this checked-in receipt. Tests use exact 11520-frame lengths, finite
samples, and maximum absolute error **1/32768**, fixed before decoder results
were inspected. They never widen the threshold or permute reference channels.

Actual encoded TOC coverage:

| Cases | Actual packet modes | Pre-skip |
| --- | --- | --- |
| silk-1 / silk-2 | 13 SILK | 312 |
| hybrid-1 / hybrid-2 | 10 Hybrid + 3 SILK | 312 |
| celt-1 / celt-2 | 13 CELT | 120 |
| mapping1-3 / mapping1-6 | 13 CELT, family 1 | 120 |

The full-channel references expose canonical channel routing bugs that a mono
mean would hide. Tests additionally mutate checksummed fixture headers to cover
pre-skip spanning packets, nonzero output gain, exact final-granule trimming
and contradictory metadata. Native workflow tests check the presented raw
values/shape, authored rescaling/resampling and actual ONNX head output.

The same CELT stereo packets are remuxed unchanged into `unsupported-opus.webm`
and `unsupported-opus.mp4`; ffprobe confirms Opus, 48 kHz, two channels in actual
Matroska/WebM and ISO MP4 containers. Tests require explicit presentation-capability
rejection before decoder construction. Their actual stream-copy commands and
SHA-256 hashes are recorded in `manifest.json`.

This small synthetic matrix establishes these numerical paths; it does not
claim full RFC conformance, recognition quality or production performance.


The `*.webm` positive fixtures are actual FFmpeg stream copies of the unchanged
Ogg Opus packets, generated by `generate_webm.py`. Their original coarse container
timestamps and final BlockDuration remain intact. `webm-manifest.json` records
actual hashes and independent libopus decode comparisons against unchanged
full-channel references (fixed 1/32768 tolerance). The historical filename
`unsupported-opus.webm` is retained as an additional original-producer positive
regression fixture; MP4 remains unsupported for its distinct header/edit convention.
